newsitem.title: BULGARIA: TELECOM JOINT VENTURE TO INVEST $30 MLN IN BULGARIA.
newsitem.headline: TELECOM JOINT VENTURE TO INVEST $30 MLN IN BULGARIA.

text.p: Bulfon, a Bulgarian-Greek telecom joint venture, plans to invest more than $30 million by the year 2000 in the development of Bulgaria's nationwide card phone system, a senior official said on Wednesday.

Pericles Katsioulas, managing director of the Greek grouping of companies Intrakom, which holds 68 percent in the venture, said that Bulfon had installed so far more than 2,500 phone card machines in 34 towns in Bulgaria.
"For this purpose Bulfon have invested $6.2 million and have supplied telecom equipment for transmission systems to the Bulgarian Telecommunications Company," Katsoulas told Reuters.
"We plan to invest another $30 million by the end of 1999, installing 25,000 phone card machines and thus completing the establishment of the nationwide card phone system," he added.

The establishment of the Bulfon venture has sparked a row in local media because the state-owned Bulgarian Telecommunications Company held only 32 percent of the venture, while Intrakom held the majority stake.
However, Bulgaria's Court of Appeal on Wednesday rejected an appeal by the Prosecutor's office against the registration of the Bulfon venture by Sofia City Court in November 1995.
The Procecutor's office has claimed that the registration has been done in violation of several local regulations.
